Hello Voat Linux Gamers,

I'm the admin of a little steam group called Steam-ALT, and I'd like to raise some awareness about that little group (and it's curator list!)

History

I'm the admin of a little steam group called Steam-ALT - or SALT - (Steam Anti-Linux Team), I'm also an active member of Steam-LUG - or SLUG - (Steam Linux User Group). Steam-Alt was born out of a joke in a game of Guns of Icarus with other SLUG members. We were on a bit of a winning streak and one of us jokingly said that no one could stop us now, to which I jokingly replied salt still could (Guns of Icarus clan names are a maximum of four letters) and then elaborated by saying [SALT] would be the Steam Anti-Linux Team. A few days later I made Steam-ALT, wrote a very ironic about page and didn't do anything with it for a while. I've since gradually started using it's curator page to document my experiences with Linux games.

I am in no way trying to compete with SLUG, I love SLUG and participate multiple times a week in their events during the holidays. If you don't know SLUG (I'd be surprised), look them up: https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamlug/

Why should I care?

I've been putting some work in the Curator page, documenting experiences I've had with Linux games. I use (-) for negative (+) for positive and (+/-) when I find it hard to say.

I include:

  • Performance
  • Bugs (linux related)
  • Gameplay (this of course is highly subjective!)

I have 3 pc's at home (Intel + NVidia, AMD + ATI, Intel + Intel) of which the first two are suited for gaming, unfortunately I study abroad and only take one with me, so I may not always be able to test it on multiple before adding a recommendation.

Future plans

A gaming channel that I will be using for extended reviews and first impressions is something I'm working on these holidays. I am having some issues with video editing on Linux atm, if you know some good documentation: feel free to tell me!

Link

Feel free to have a look, and maybe join ^^

https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamalt/
Steam-alt : The ironic steam group for Linux gamers
